questions.stem: Aplicando «Use a negative exclamation in context / Surprise. / A fixed exclamation built on a negative» al texto, ¿cuál de las opciones se sostiene?
questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: what settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: no me digas!' expresses surprise or disbelief. On that basis "Surprise or disbelief" is the supported choice. Option A ("A command to stop speaking") fails because it confuses exclamation with imperative; Option C ("A question about speaking") fails because it confuses exclamation with interrogative; Option D ("An affirmation") fails because it confuses negative with affirmative.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Applying the negative rules to a short exchange
questions.learningObjective: Apply negation in a short exchange in context

stimulus.body: El fragmento siguiente sirve para comprobar la comprensión de esta forma. Cuatro opciones responden a él, y una sola concuerda con los datos de la nota.

questions.stem: Con la pista «Apply negation in a short exchange in context / Correct with the positive. / Applying the negative rules to a short exchange», ¿qué opción se ajusta realmente al fragmento?

options.misconception: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: after a negative answer, a corrected positive statement follows. On that basis "With a corrected positive statement" is the supported choice. Option A ("With a question") fails because it confuses exchange with question; Option B ("With another negative") fails because it reverses the direction of the reasoning that settles applying the negative rules to a short exchange; Option D ("With silence") fails because it avoids the correction.
